questions.question: / to assess the environmental impact of a soap bar throughout its entire life cycle, from raw material sourcing to packaging disposal. The study covered four stages: raw materials, manufacturing, packaging and transportation, and use and disposal. The LCA showed that the raw material stage, particularly palm oil cultivation, contributed significantly to the product’s environmental impact due to land and water use. This highlighted impacts that were not apparent when the company focused mainly on factory operations. Based on the findings, the company began working with certified sustainable palm oil suppliers and reduced plastic in some packaging. Questions: a) Define Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) based on the case. b) Explain the four stages examined in the LCA of the soap bar. c) Analyse why the raw material stage had a significant environmental impact. d) Evaluate how the LCA findings influenced Godrej’s procurement and packaging decisions.

questions.question: A manufacturing company imports critical raw materials through a major / international port. A prolonged port closure causes shipments to stop for several weeks. Production begins to decline, and emergency transportation through an alternative port becomes necessary. Management wants to develop a more resilient sourcing and logistics strategy. (i) Identify the vulnerabilities exposed by the disruption. (5 marks) (ii) Explain how business continuity planning could have reduced the impact. (5 marks) (iii) Suggest alternative logistics and sourcing arrangements. (5 marks) (iv) Recommend long-term resilience measures for the company. (5 marks)
